title: Vientiane International Marathon 2026 Review: Laos's Rare Full Marathon in the Cool-Season Capital
seo_title: Vientiane International Marathon 2026 Review: Course, Tips & Guide
meta_description: Comprehensive Vientiane International Marathon 2026 review: a full marathon in Laos, one of Southeast Asia's rarest race destinations. December 6 at Saphangmo, Vientiane. 42K, 21K, 10K, and 5K in cool dry-season conditions.
dek: A full marathon in Laos — a country with one of the smallest road-race calendars in Southeast Asia — held on December 6, 2026, at the Saphangmo venue in the capital Vientiane. With four distances from 42.195 km down to 5 km, cool dry-season morning temperatures in the mid-teens Celsius, and the novelty of racing in a nation that most runners have never pinned a bib in, this is one of the most genuinely rare marathon propositions in the region.
verdict: The Vientiane International Marathon earns its place on any serious Southeast Asian runner's radar for one reason above all: it is a full marathon in Laos, a country where the entire annual road-race calendar can be counted on one hand. For runners who collect country ticks — or who simply want to experience a marathon in a place that has not been flattened by the mass-participation industry — Laos offers something that Singapore, Bangkok, and Kuala Lumpur cannot. The December 6 date is well-chosen: this is the cool, dry season in Vientiane, with morning temperatures in the mid-teens Celsius, low humidity by Southeast Asian standards, and virtually no rain — conditions that rival Chiang Mai or Hanoi as the best marathon weather in the region. The Saphangmo venue, on the outskirts of the capital along the Mekong River, provides a flat, fast course canvas with views across to Thailand on the opposite bank. The event offers the full distance suite (42K, 21K, 10K, 5K), making it accessible to serious marathoners and casual participants alike. The caveats are real and should not be brushed aside: the reliability score is low (20), the organiser is not clearly identified on the official website, and registration has not yet opened for the 2026 edition. Past editions of the Vientiane Marathon have been small-scale affairs — fields in the hundreds rather than thousands — with the production values and on-course support that you would expect from a nascent event in a developing race market. For runners who can tolerate some organisational rough edges in exchange for a genuinely uncommon marathon experience, this is one to track closely and book once registration opens. For runners who demand the polish of a Gold Label event, wait a few more years — Laos's running scene is growing, but it is not there yet.

sections.heading: Laos: The Rarest Country Tick in Southeast Asian Running
paragraphs: Laos has one of the smallest road-race calendars in Southeast Asia — a handful of events in Vientiane, a half marathon in Luang Prabang, and not much else [1]. For runners who track the countries they have raced in, Laos is one of the hardest boxes to check in the region: there are more marathons in a single Thai province than in the entire country of Laos [2].

This scarcity is not due to a lack of interest — the Vientiane running community is small but active, and the Luang Prabang Half Marathon (Run for Children) has been running for years and draws a modest but loyal international field [2]. The constraint is infrastructure: road closures, medical support, timing systems, and the organisational ecosystem that supports mass-participation running are still developing in Laos [2].

For the runner who values novelty and is willing to accept that a marathon in Laos will not feel like a marathon in Singapore, the Vientiane International Marathon offers something genuinely rare: the chance to run 42 kilometres through one of the least-visited running destinations in the world [1].

sections.heading: The Course: Saphangmo and the Mekong Riverside
paragraphs: The race is based at Saphangmo, a district on the southeastern edge of Vientiane along the Mekong River [1]. The Mekong forms the border between Laos and Thailand at this point, and the riverfront setting provides a flat, scenic backdrop — views across the water to the Thai town of Sri Chiang Mai, fishing boats on the river, and the wide, open skies of the Mekong floodplain [2].

The course is flat — Vientiane sits on the Mekong alluvial plain, and the elevation change across 42 kilometres is negligible [2]. For marathoners, this means the course itself is fast; the limiting factor will be the climate (even in December, Vientiane can warm up quickly after sunrise) and the on-course support (aid station frequency and medical coverage are likely to be sparser than at a major-city marathon) [1].

The full marathon route is likely to be an out-and-back or loop course along the riverside roads, possibly extending into the Vientiane city centre — past the Patuxai Victory Monument, the That Luang stupa, or along the tree-lined boulevards of the capital's French-colonial quarter [2]. The official course map for the 2026 edition has not been published, but the geography of Vientiane — flat, compact, and river-oriented — limits the range of plausible routes [1].

sections.heading: December in Vientiane: The Best Running Weather in Southeast Asia?
paragraphs: December is the peak of the cool, dry season in Laos — the northeast monsoon brings cool, dry air from the Asian continent, and Vientiane enjoys some of the most comfortable running conditions in Southeast Asia [3]. Morning temperatures typically range from 14–18°C, rising to the mid-20s by late morning, with humidity significantly lower than during the May–October wet season [3].

For marathoners, these conditions are close to ideal: a 5:00am start would allow runners to complete the majority of the race in temperatures under 20°C, with the sun rising around 6:30am and temperatures climbing gradually through the morning [3]. This stands in stark contrast to marathons in Singapore, Bangkok, or Ho Chi Minh City, where even December mornings start warm and get hotter [3].

Rain is virtually unheard of in Vientiane in December — this is the driest month of the year, with average rainfall of less than 5mm [3]. For runners who have been rained on at enough Southeast Asian races to develop a superstition about it, this alone is worth the trip [3].

sections.heading: Registration, Logistics, and What to Expect
paragraphs: Registration for the 2026 edition has not yet opened through the official website at vientianemarathon.com [1]. Past editions have offered tiered pricing with early-bird rates — expect marathon entry fees in the USD 40–70 range for international runners, with lower rates for Lao residents and ASEAN nationals [1].

Vientiane is served by Wattay International Airport (VTE), with direct flights from Bangkok, Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, Kuala Lumpur, and Kunming [2]. From the airport, Saphangmo is approximately a 20-minute taxi or tuk-tuk ride. Accommodation in Vientiane ranges from backpacker guesthouses (USD 10–20/night) to mid-range hotels (USD 30–60/night) along the Mekong riverfront — book early, as December is the peak tourist season in Laos [2].

Race-day logistics: expect a small field (hundreds, not thousands), a low-key start area, manual or basic chip timing, and aid stations that may offer water and bananas rather than the electrolyte smorgasbord of a major-city marathon [1]. Bring your own nutrition — gels, salt tablets, and any specific fuelling you rely on — as the on-course provisions should be treated as a supplement, not a primary source. A post-race meal of Lao food (larb, sticky rice, and a cold Beerlao by the Mekong) is one of the better finisher experiences in world marathoning [2].

sections.heading: Should You Run the Vientiane International Marathon?
paragraphs: If you collect country ticks or are chasing a marathon in every Southeast Asian nation: this is your Laos opportunity, and it is a good one — full marathon distance, cool December weather, flat course, and a capital-city setting that is genuinely charming rather than merely functional [1]. Book once registration opens and treat the organisational quirks as part of the adventure [1].

If you are a marathon tourist looking for a unique cultural experience: Vientiane delivers. The city is walkable, the food is excellent, the French-colonial architecture is well-preserved, and the Mekong sunset is worth the trip alone [2]. A marathon weekend here doubles as a cultural holiday in a way that a race in a concrete metropolis does not [2].

If you demand Gold Label production values, corral starts, and aid stations every two kilometres with precision-timed electrolyte distribution: wait a few more years. The Vientiane International Marathon is a developing event in a developing race market — it will not match the polish of Singapore or Bangkok [1]. But for the right runner, that is precisely the point [1].

faqs.question: When and where is the Vientiane International Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: The race is scheduled for Sunday, December 6, 2026, at the Saphangmo venue in Vientiane, the capital of Laos. Saphangmo is a district on the southeastern edge of the city along the Mekong River, approximately 20 minutes from Wattay International Airport.

faqs.question: What distances are offered at the Vientiane International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Four distances are available: a full marathon (42.195 km), a half marathon (21.1 km), a 10K, and a 5K. The full marathon is the headline event, but the multi-distance format makes the race accessible to runners of all levels.

faqs.question: What are the race-day conditions like in Vientiane in December?
faqs.answer: December is the cool, dry season in Vientiane — morning temperatures range from 14–18°C with low humidity, rising to the mid-20s by late morning. Rain is virtually non-existent (less than 5mm average monthly rainfall). These are among the best marathon conditions in Southeast Asia.

faqs.question: How do I register and what should I expect on race day?
faqs.answer: Registration is through the official website at vientianemarathon.com, though the 2026 edition window has not yet opened. Expect marathon entry fees in the USD 40–70 range. Race-day expectations: a small field (hundreds, not thousands), basic to moderate on-course support, and flat terrain. Bring your own nutrition as a primary source and treat on-course provisions as a supplement.

faqs.question: Is the Vientiane International Marathon worth travelling for?
faqs.answer: For country-tick collectors, marathon tourists seeking unique cultural experiences, and runners who value novelty over polish: absolutely — a full marathon in Laos in cool December weather is a genuinely rare proposition. For runners who demand Gold Label production standards: this is a developing event in a developing race market, and you may want to wait a few years.
